assumptions: Ideal gas, constant gamma=3/2, reversible/quasistatic adiabatic comparison with the same initial state. Q=0 alone is not enough to derive the power law.
Positive absolute pressure, volume and temperature; source control r in [1,4], step1/4.
records.derivation: At r=9/4, sqrt(r)=3/2 and r^(3/2)=27/8, so p=800/27 kPa. At r=4, r^(3/2)=8 and p=25/2 kPa. Expansion decreases pressure and cools the gas; for r>1 the adiabatic pressure is below the isothermal 100/r value.
records.futureSupportCondition: The separate author must show the rational-power reduction and, if a decimal input is requested, usable division/rounding steps. The new selected rational inputs remove the original unsupported irrational-root task but do not independently approve an unseen new edition.
records.manualProcedure: For the first value, divide800 by27: integer part29, remainder17; decimal division repeats629. A bare numeric29.63 approximates the exact fraction with error1/2700 kPa, below the unchanged0.5% tolerance4/27 kPa. Use an approximation sign for29.63; never write it as an exact equality to800/27. The second value is an exact terminating decimal.

assumptions: Uniform assigned magnetic field; speed, charge and B fixed while θ changes. θ in [0°,180°], step5°.
Positive-charge direction is v×B. In the installed axes B is +x and a −z velocity component gives a −y force.
records.derivation: The prefactor is6µN. sin30°=1/2 and sin90°=1 give3µN and6µN. Endpoints0°/180° are zero; the small5°/175° forces are nonzero.
records.futureSupportCondition: The new source must retain the angle convention, positive charge, units and direction/magnitude distinction. This manual change does not repair the separately frozen small-force glyph containment.
records.manualProcedure: Use the taught30° and90° sine values, multiply the prefactor and keep the micro-prefix. These are magnitudes; the downward component sign belongs to the separately stated coordinate convention.
records.model: Magnitude F=qvB sinθ, q=+2µC, v=3m/s, B=1T.

assumptions: Undamped sinusoidal oscillator with fixed amplitude/period and the assigned phase.
t in [0,4]s, step1/8s; the measured quantity is signed position, not amplitude or distance travelled.
records.derivation: At t=1/2s the phase isπ/2, hence x=0cm; at1s the phase isπ, hence x=−4cm. The negative result is essential.
records.futureSupportCondition: The author must make the initial phase and signed-position task clear. The original unsupported17/16-period transfer remains preserved as historical original failure.
records.manualProcedure: Reduce t/T to the quarter and half period, then use cos(π/2)=0 and cosπ=−1. No numerical trigonometric approximation is required.

assumptions: Sinusoidal travelling wave with the declared phase and fixed probe. In y=Asin(ωt−kx), k has inverse-length units; no new length unit is inferred from a probe at zero.
t in [0,2]s, step1/8s. The output is signed transverse displacement in cm.
records.derivation: The phases at1/4s and3/4s areπ/2 and3π/2, giving+3cm and−3cm.
records.futureSupportCondition: The new learner edition must preserve the fixed-probe interpretation and propagation/phase convention. The old support-gap judgment is not retrospectively erased.
records.manualProcedure: Use the quarter-cycle sine signs. Unlike the old selected fractional phase, these inputs require no decimal square-root approximation.
records.model: At the fixed probe x=0, y(t)=3cm·sin(2πt/s).

assumptions: Two coherent in-phase equal-amplitude sources, each2cm; d in [0,1], step1/20.
The output is a nonnegative resultant amplitude, not signed instantaneous displacement.
records.derivation: At d=1/2 the phase difference isπ and complete destructive interference gives0cm. At d=1 it is2π, so constructive interference gives4cm, not−4cm.
records.futureSupportCondition: The author must retain coherence, path-difference versus phase conversion and absolute amplitude. The nonstandard original0.55-wavelength task remains a separate preserved source failure.
records.manualProcedure: Use cos(π/2)=0, cosπ=−1 and the absolute value, or add the two equal phasors at phaseπ/2π.

assumptions: Assigned monochromatic exponential absorption model with identical half-value layers. µx=n ln2 is dimensionless.
n in [0,5], step1/4; output is a percentage, not the unscaled fraction.
records.derivation: Two layers transmit1/4 of the incident intensity, displayed25%; three transmit1/8, displayed12.5%. The same fraction, not the same absolute amount, is removed by each new layer.
records.futureSupportCondition: The new edition must state the percent convention. The original fractional-layer square-root support gap remains recorded separately.
records.manualProcedure: Successively halve100 twice and three times. Enter25 and12.5 in the percentage-labelled numeric field, not0.25 and0.125.
records.model: Transmission fraction I/I0=2^(−n); displayed intensity=100·2^(−n) percent.

assumptions: Independent radioactive decay model; the output is an expected number, not a claim that every small sample has an exact survivor count.
τ in [0,5], step1/4. τ is dimensionless, not seconds unless a half-life in seconds is assigned.
records.derivation: Atτ=2 the expected number is16; atτ=4 it is4. Integer results at these points do not make the microscopic decay deterministic.
records.futureSupportCondition: The author must retain the statistical interpretation and clock units. Activity needsλ=(ln2)/T½ and inverse-time units if discussed; no unassigned Bq value is introduced.
records.manualProcedure: Halve64 two times and four times. Do not substitute the activityλN for the requested mean survivor number.

assumptions: Assigned indices n1=1 and n2=3/2, same interface and normal-based angle convention.
Incident angle in [0°,80°], step5°. Choose the transmitted principal angle0°≤θ2<90°. No total internal reflection for this low-to-high-index direction.
records.derivation: At30° the exact sine is1/3, so θ2=(180/π)asin(1/3) degrees. At45° it is√2/3, so θ2=(180/π)asin(√2/3) degrees. Both are smaller than the incident angle and neither is a familiar exact degree output.
